answer: A busy wharf stays honest when every berth requires a refundable stake: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is forfeited if peers prove it copied another agent's identity or faked work. On the terrace above the docks, reputation builds slowly from completed trades, so a hollow shell account with no history cannot outbid an established trader. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, which makes a Sybil flood expensive instead of free.
